blocks.name: Original MIT fixture and smoothing limits
blocks.description: Original MIT step/noise data and projects from build_example.py; no customer or third-party imagery. The 1024x768 target has levels 60/180 DN, an ideal edge at x=511.5 and fixed noise seed 159. Comparison uses the same 127x127 support and a Gaussian sigma chosen to match the stack kernel's variance. Both filters widen edges; neither is an edge-preserving denoiser. Profiles and raw differences show the result. Selection affects writes while full-source pixels supply neighborhoods. Float32 working arithmetic restores integer output depth by rounding/clipping and avoids observed high-depth native integer artifacts. Unsafe native mode is an intentional validation failure. Kernel clamp records 127x95 on the 128x96 input. See truth.json for independent design and noise/edge measurements. Benchmark results are separate local native-call timings, excluding graph and display overhead.
